title: Casimir-Electrostatic NEMS Pull-In: Bifurcation, Phase Diagrams & Physics-Informed Neural Networks
description:
Reproducible computational archive accompanying the article "Casimir-Electrostatic Pull-In in Nanomechanical Actuators: Phase Diagrams, Design Sensitivities, and Physics-Informed Neural-Network Surrogates" (Physical Review Applied, in preparation, 2026).

The code models the pull-in instability of a parallel-plate nano-electromechanical (NEMS) oscillator driven by both an electrostatic force and the attractive Casimir force. It (i) derives the closed-form saddle-node (fold) bifurcation separating the stable and pull-in regimes in the (electrostatic, Casimir) control plane, (ii) maps the dynamic pull-in phase diagram by deterministic Runge-Kutta integration from rest, (iii) trains physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that solve the governing ODE, including a pull-in-safe rapidity parametrization for the movable pole and a parametric PINN that learns the fold boundary purely from the force-balance residual, and (iv) computes the finite-temperature Lifshitz correction and the resulting thermal shift of the pull-in voltage. All results, models, logs and the six publication figures regenerate deterministically from a single fixed seed (42), CPU-only, in float64. See README.md and SEEDS.md.
